heroHeadline: DOGE Formally Disbanded; Judge Blocks $1.8B Anti-Weaponization Fund; US-Iran Tentative 60-Day Ceasefire Extension Drafted — Day 497
heroSubtitle: On May 30-31, 2026 (Days 496-497 of Trump's second term), two major Trump-era institutions reached pivotal moments: DOGE was formally disbanded after Elon Musk's Special Government Employee contract expired (functions absorbed by OPM; $215B+ in claimed savings disputed by Cato/GAO), and a federal judge temporarily blocked Trump's $1.8 billion Anti-Weaponization Fund. On the Iran front, the US and Iran reached a tentative framework on May 29 for a 60-day ceasefire extension and Strait of Hormuz reopening — but Trump toughened terms on May 30 (demanding Iran destroy 440.9 kg of highly enriched uranium) then further tightened them on May 31, telling CBS News he is 'in no hurry' to close a deal. Trump also signed an EO restoring off-road vehicle access to federal lands by rescinding Nixon- and Carter-era restrictions. Multiple polls released through May 31 show Trump's approval at aggregate second-term lows: Silver Bulletin net -19.1, Economist/YouGov 34%, and a record -47 net approval on inflation. Senate Republicans face growing internal pressure over the Anti-Weaponization Fund, with several senators proposing legislation to add congressional oversight.
